original_question: Fix 0 <= k <= binom(n,2), let lambda and mu be partitions of length at most n with mu contained in lambda, and define the symmetric function t_{lambda/mu,k} = (-1)^k sum_{w in S_n, ell(w) >= k} epsilon_w h_{lambda + delta - w(mu + delta)}. Is there a natural combinatorial interpretation of the scalar product <t_{lambda/mu,k}, s_nu>?
target_in_paper: Section 2 (Problems of 2025), Problem 26, which records [Stan1999, Ch. 7 Exer. 38(b)]: the open problem asking for a nice combinatorial interpretation of the scalar product ⟨t_{λ/μ,k}, s_ν⟩, where t_{λ/μ,k} is the truncation of the Jacobi–Trudi expansion of s_{λ/μ} obtained by keeping only terms with ℓ(w) ≥ k.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It fixes k in the same range, takes λ and μ to be partitions of length at most n with μ contained in λ, defines the same truncated Jacobi–Trudi sum t_{λ/μ,k}, and asks for a combinatorial interpretation of the scalar product with a Schur function s_ν.
missing_details: The paper's problem is not fully stand-alone unless the ambient symmetric-function ring is specified; one should say that t_{λ/μ,k}, h_r, and s_ν live in the ring Λ of symmetric functions (typically over Q or Z) in infinitely many variables.
The scalar product should be identified explicitly as the Hall inner product on Λ.
The vector δ must be defined explicitly as δ = (n−1, n−2, ..., 1, 0).
The sign ε_w should be defined explicitly as sgn(w).
The statistic ℓ(w) should be defined explicitly as the inversion number (equivalently, Coxeter length) of w ∈ S_n.
Because λ and μ are only said to have length at most n, they should be regarded as n-tuples by appending trailing zeros before forming λ + δ − w(μ + δ).
The notation h_{λ+δ−w(μ+δ)} needs to be unpacked: for an integer vector α = (α_1, ..., α_n), one should define h_α = ∏_i h_{α_i}, together with the standard conventions h_0 = 1 and h_r = 0 for r < 0.
The quantifier on ν is implicit in the draft; to make the question stand-alone, one should ask for all partitions ν of the relevant degree.
The degree restriction is implicit: t_{λ/μ,k} is homogeneous of degree |λ|−|μ|, so only partitions ν with |ν| = |λ|−|μ| are relevant.
The containment notation μ ⊆ λ should be clarified as Ferrers/Young-diagram containment.
refined_question:
Let Λ = Sym_Q be the ring of symmetric functions in variables x_1, x_2, ... equipped with the Hall inner product ⟨·,·⟩. Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and an integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ binom(n,2). Let λ and μ be partitions of length at most n with μ ⊆ λ, and regard them as elements of Z^n by appending trailing zeros. Set δ := (n−1, n−2, ..., 1, 0). For w ∈ S_n, let ℓ(w) be its inversion number and ε_w := sgn(w). For α = (α_1, ..., α_n) ∈ Z^n, define h_α := ∏_{i=1}^n h_{α_i}, with the standard conventions h_0 = 1 and h_r = 0 for r < 0. Define

t_{λ/μ,k} := (−1)^k ∑_{w∈S_n, ℓ(w)≥k} ε_w h_{λ+δ−w(μ+δ)}.

This is the truncation of the Jacobi–Trudi expansion of the skew Schur function s_{λ/μ} obtained by keeping only those terms indexed by permutations w with ℓ(w) ≥ k. Since t_{λ/μ,k} is homogeneous of degree |λ|−|μ|, ask for each partition ν of |λ|−|μ|: is there a nice combinatorial interpretation of the Hall inner product ⟨t_{λ/μ,k}, s_ν⟩?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the paper's Problem 26, so the correct refinement is not to broaden it but only to make the standard symmetric-function notation explicit. Problem 26 states exactly this truncation-of-Jacobi–Trudi question and does not supply a different theorem, conjecture, or equivalent reformulation elsewhere in the paper. The additions in the refined version—ambient ring, Hall inner product, the definition of δ, the meaning of ε_w and ℓ(w), zero-padding of λ and μ, the convention for h_α, and the degree restriction on ν—are precisely the implicit data needed to make the problem mathematically self-contained while staying faithful to the printed statement.
